_note: Card scenes: the pool. One scene for every real card, grouped under the tag of the card it was written for, its first tag. `scenes` is keyed by scene id; `card` is a suggestion, not a binding, and any card may end up with any scene. Scenes with a `from` keep a round-2 subject word for word; the rest are new. `adversary`, `discord` and `unity` are no card tags and their cards have no frame yet, so those groups hold only the scenes in a batch. A draw is `preamble`, `emphasis`, `lighting`, `framing`, the subject, then the tag's `accent`: `preamble` mixes round 2's styles C and E, `emphasis` is what stops a draw reading as a photograph, `framing` keeps the subject inside the middle 76% the building window crops to. `batch` is the current draw list: scene id to the two real cards it is composited on, one program or event and one building, so each scene is seen in both art windows; for the groups with no frame they are the nearest fit by name. Earlier batches are in picks/scene_batch_<n>.json, whose row ids are the scenes already drawn.
preamble: Stylised painterly board-game illustration in textured gouache, simplified forms and clean brush shapes, visible paper grain, soft clear warm natural light, moderately saturated palette, a confident silhouette with crisp detail on the subject and loose backgrounds, near-future setting: clean modern machinery, clothes and buildings, never historical.
emphasis: A hand-painted illustration on a board-game box, never a photograph or a 3D render: matte opaque paint, broad visible brush shapes, few details, large simple masses grouped by colour, dry brush texture and paper grain everywhere, no glossy reflections.
lighting: Mid-key lighting, even daylight or clear interior light, never night-dark or blown-out; the scene's tag colour as its accent; a strong silhouette that reads at card size. No text, logos, UI, or close-up faces.
framing: Keep the whole subject inside the middle two-thirds of the image height: only plain floor, ceiling or sky in the top and bottom sixths, nothing important there.
